questions.question: What is a fuel, and what does a fuel need to start and keep burning? Give two fire safety rules.
questions.expected_answer: A fuel is a material that stores energy, which is released as heat and light when it burns; examples are coal, wood, paraffin, gas, candle wax and, for our bodies, food. A fuel needs heat to ignite it and oxygen to keep burning. Safety rules include standing candles in a tin of sand, never filling a paraffin stove while it burns, keeping matches away from small children, and, in a fire, getting out, staying low and calling 10177 or 112.

questions.question: Explain how a bulb in a circuit lights up and how a coal-fired power station makes electricity.
questions.expected_answer: A cell stores energy. When the cell, wires and bulb form a complete circuit, electrical energy is transferred from the cell to the bulb, which changes it into light and heat. In a power station, burning coal boils water into steam, the steam spins a turbine, and the turbine turns a generator that makes electricity. The electricity travels along power lines in a circuit to our homes and back.

questions.question: How do elastic and springs store energy, and what happens when they are released?
questions.expected_answer: Elastic stores energy when it is stretched or twisted, and a spring stores energy when it is compressed or stretched. The more it is stretched, twisted or squashed, the more energy it stores, up to a limit. When it is released, the stored energy changes into movement energy, as in a catapult, a wind-up toy or a cotton-reel tractor.
